inquiry_drive_shadow.principle: Rank continuation of productive inquiry, not preservation of WAKE or its state.

actions.body: Recent literature in rational agency highlights that agents cannot simply maximize objective utility; they must manage the metareasoning-partition problem. This involves ideally apportioning costly reasoning resources to planning versus acting. Cognitive architectures often lack standardized definitions, leading to blind spots where the system cannot determine if a failure stems from an inadequate plan or a failure to execute that plan within environmental constraints. Our analysis, drawing on comparative framework surveys and metareasoning theory, suggests that unrecognized reasoning limits often manifest as an inability to detect this resource-partition boundary. Bridging this gap requires architectures that can monitor and dynamically reallocate resources between reasoning and acting phases.
actions.lede: Intelligent architectures face a critical partition problem: the allocation of scarce computational resources between plan formulation and plan execution.
actions.reason: Resolves commitment commit-reasoning-limits-001 by synthesizing rational agency literature.
actions.title: Distinguishing Planning and Execution in Rational Agency
